title: Video by preachcinemaa
description:
🎥🎬: Lazarus (2025)

Set in the year 2052, the world appears to have entered a golden age thanks to a miracle drug called Hapna. Developed by the brilliant neuroscientist Dr. Skinner, the drug eliminates pain and disease, making it one of the greatest medical breakthroughs in history. After releasing Hapna, Skinner mysteriously disappears, and humanity embraces the drug without question.

Three years later, Skinner suddenly reappears with a terrifying announcement: Hapna was never truly safe. He reveals that everyone who has taken the drug is doomed to die when its effects expire, and the first deaths will begin in just thirty days. Since billions of people have used Hapna, the entire world faces extinction. 

In response, a special task force known as Lazarus is assembled. The team consists of five highly skilled but unconventional agents, including the talented escape artist Axel Gilberto, hacker Eleina, and several other specialists. Their mission is simple but nearly impossible: find Dr. Skinner before time runs out and force him to reveal a cure. 

As Lazarus races across the globe, they uncover conspiracies, corruption, and hidden truths behind Hapna’s creation. The team faces dangerous enemies, false leads, and growing panic as governments and corporations struggle to maintain order. Meanwhile, the countdown to humanity’s possible extinction continues. 

The series combines futuristic science fiction, mystery, stylish action, and philosophical questions about humanity’s dependence on technology and miracle solutions. Created by Shinichirō Watanabe, the show is known for its sleek animation, fast-paced action scenes, and jazz-inspired soundtrack. 

In the end, Lazarus is a high-stakes race against time in which a small group of agents must save the world from a catastrophe that humanity willingly brought upon itself.

title: Video by the_movie_patriot
description:
🎥🎬: Modest Heroes (2018)

Modest Heroes is a Japanese animated anthology by Studio Ponoc, made up of three powerful short stories that explore courage in quiet, unexpected ways.

The first story, “Kanini & Kanino,” follows two tiny crab siblings navigating a dangerous underwater world after losing their father. It’s a survival story filled with tension, showing how bravery can exist even in the smallest creatures.

Next is “Life Ain’t Gonna Lose,” centered on a young boy living with a severe egg allergy. What seems like an ordinary day quickly turns intense when his condition puts his life at risk. It’s grounded, emotional, and shows how real-life challenges can be just as heroic as any battle.

The final story, “Invisible,” follows a man who literally becomes invisible to the world—no one can see or acknowledge him. As he struggles with isolation, his journey becomes a quiet reflection on identity, purpose, and being seen in a world that overlooks you.

Each story is simple on the surface but hits deep, reminding you that not all heroes wear capes—some are just trying to survive, be understood, or keep going.

JUNKYARD KING – Episode 1 ⚔️

Following the events of Episode 0, Artie wakes up only to realize it wasn’t a dream. Whatever happened is real, and he now has to prepare for what’s coming his way.

This episode started as a simple experiment with @invideo.io Agent One and somehow turned into a full 9-minute chapter.

What I enjoyed most about the process was how much it shifted my focus away from prompt engineering and toward filmmaking. Instead of obsessing over keywords, I spent more time thinking about direction, camera angles, movement, pacing, character interactions, and dialogue. In other words, the things that actually matter when trying to tell a story.

That difference ended up being significant for me, and it’s one of the reasons I’ve been spending more time talking with the Invideo team. The product is still early, but I also think there’s a tremendous amount of potential there.

More than anything, I’m excited about where Junkyard King is heading. The world is growing, the characters are evolving, and there are still a lot of stories left to tell.

Animation PV — La Langue des Vipères

La Langue des Vipères feels less like fantasy and more like a forgotten myth whispered back to life. Created by Juliette Brocal ( @cy_lindric ), the story follows Iodis the illegitimate daughter of a cardinal learning a mysterious language tied to hidden power.
But this isn’t magic in the traditional sense. Here, language itself becomes the weapon.
 words carrying influence beyond understanding, knowledge treated as something sacred and dangerous, a medieval world where silence can be safer than speaking.

The animated trailer by @potto.collective captures that atmosphere beautifully  dreamlike and deeply intimate. Every frame feels like an illuminated manuscript brought to life, where beauty hides tension underneath it. And that’s what makes the concept so compelling.

Because La Langue des Vipères isn’t asking whether magic exists. It asks who gets to control it and what happens when forbidden knowledge finds the wrong voice. In a world shaped by power and secrecy, words become more than communication they become destiny itself.

description:

No calls, no paperwork.

How to use it in a real workflow?

• test different materials on a character before going to production
• try different color schemes
• render a character for a pitch or presentation

description:
Agent venom vs Carnage! FAN Animation!

This was loads of fun to make, my longest fan animation so far! I recently got to watch a video by a @comicstorian where he talked about why agent venom is his favorite super hero. Seeing the character through his eyes really got me excited to make this animation. I wanted to really stick with his military roots as I made this animation. I really wanted to feel different than Peter or anyone else with similar abilities. Even with his use of webs I tried to include a military mindset to show more of Flash under the mask and wanted to hint at the struggles that came with his military injuries at the end.

Of course the best villain for Agent Venom or any Venom had to be Carnage! Carnage is also one of my favorite villains, I always wanted to animate him! Huge Thanks to @told_by_3 for this amazing model and rig.

❤️When Great Animation Has Hear❤️

When you are good at something, it does not matter if you work on feature films or TV. The work shines no matter what.

James Baxter is proof of that. From Quasimodo in Disney Hunchback to a horse balancing on a ball in Adventure Time, the craft and the heart are always there.

This scene from Steven Universe is one of the most touching moments I have seen in animation. It has so much emotion, and it was animated exactly that way. With honesty, clarity, and feeling.

Even as a veteran animator, scenes like this still inspire me. They remind us, whether you are just starting out or have been doing this for years, of the deep effect 2D animation can have on people.

title: Video by edisontoonsart
description:
2D animation is not the past. It’s the foundation.

Before a 3D character ever moves on screen, it has to act.
And that acting often starts in 2D.

Here’s a great example from Moana.
This is a 2D reference scene animated by the great Randy Haycock, created to help guide the 3D animators.

Why does this matter?

Because 2D animation strips things down to their essentials:
timing, rhythm, clarity, weight, appeal, and emotion.
It’s pure performance, no rendering, no shaders, no shortcuts.

3D animation doesn’t replace that.
It stands on it.

This kind of 2D reference helps 3D animators find the heart of a scene before translating it into volume and space. It’s one of the reasons great animation still feels alive, believable, and human.

Different tools. Same principles.
Good animation is good animation.

If you love animation craft, process, and character acting,
please follow, like, and share to help keep this conversation alive.

title: Video by blind_mind_sa
description:
So... Gumball!!! As you know I worked on the TWWWOG, and I'm super excited to show you all some of my work during my last year on @studio.soi ! 

I had to do the Key Animation for this shot from The Homework episode... WHAT A CHALLENGING SHOT! It's almost 900 frames!! And there are sooo many points to deal with! Not only the exhausted acting of Gumball, losing his weight every two seconds, but also having his feet tracking the 3D moving background were important issues to keep in mind while planning the shot. Keeping consistent volumes of every appearing prop was also a big thing to deal with!

Needless to say, the shot was a reference to the wonderful short film "Afternoon Class" by Seoro Oh, which was a huge inspiration while animating it. 

To be honest, I still see some little things that I would change in terms of animation, but I did what I could with the time that I got, so I'm proud of the result! The Key animation team usually took one or two weeks per episode but for only this shot I took a WHOLE MONTH to do the rough animation. FUN FACT☝️🤓: because of that I was the only Key Animator of the team who didn't work on The Amadain episode. (Well it's more a sad fact than a fun fact tho xd)

Honestly, when @freddieelsom assigned me this shot, I couldn't believe it; it was such a shot to live up to! I remember he told me it was almost a full animation exercise! Indeed it was, I learned sooo much animating it! So thank you, Freddie, for trusting me with such an amzing task, I'm so grateful for that <3

But of course this is not a one-person-job shot, as we all know in this industry everything is thanks to ✨TEAM WORK✨ I could enhance my animation thanks to design references (by the amazing @puddlefisher), storyboard poses, and of course, retakes. The clean up and inbetweening were all done by the mervelous @bluestroke_ (no sé cómo no me mataste xd) The FX animation was thanks to the fantastic @milgonc ! 

I dont know who was in charge of the spectacular Comp, so please let me know who I'm missing so I can give them credit for their magnificent work!

I will be posting more interesting stuff soon... Apa, siau!

title: Video by pointlessergio
description:
A really weird one from somewhere around eleven or twelve years ago.
@tomdelonge asked me to create a parody animation of ET discovering his shiny finger powers for a product launch he was doing at the time.
The directions were something like: make it funny dumb pathetic silly awkward (can't remember the exact wording)

I animated it in Flash, which felt pretty limited next to the 2D tools we have today.
The whole thing took about three or four weeks from start to finish.

It's interesting to look back and see how many things I'd do differently nowadays.

Huge thanks to @mygla for the amazing post production. She made it look super nice 🙌
